PASTHIST.DESC:
From 2007 to September 2017, I held various leadership positions at Walgreens. The most recent was District manager where I oversaw the front end and pharmacy operation of 14 locations. Prior to that I was district pharmacy supervisor where I oversaw 24 locations but only the pharmacy department. 
I was in charge or hiring and developing talent, opening or closing new locations, conducting buy outs and ensuring that the pharmacy and front end operated to the highest standards. I ensured policies and procedures were properly followed and our pharmacist practiced at the top of their license. While doing this my team had the highest engagement and performance rankings and our customers the highest satisfaction scores.

MEMBER.NAME: Texas Pharmacy Association
MEMBER.DESC:
TPA "unifies, strengthens, and protects the profession of pharmacy in Texas."
It is the primary professional organization for all Texas pharmacy professionals (pharmacists, technicians, students) that advocates for the profession, advances patient care, and unifies the field through legislative efforts, continuing education (CE), networking, and resources, serving diverse settings like community, hospital, and long-term care. TPA works at the state level to influence policy, provides essential tools like advocacy toolkits, publishes industry news, and offers career support, aiming to elevate the role of pharmacists in improving public health.

The perceptions of Hispanic college students with disabilities towards diet and exercise: Generating theory to support sustainable solutions for health promotion
CONGRANT.SPONORG: National Institute on Disability, Independent Living, and Rehabilitation Research (NIDILRR)

CONGRANT.TITLE: "The Perceptions of Hispanic College Students with Disabilities Toward Diet and Exercise"
CONGRANT.SPONORG: Langston University, Langston's Rehabilitation Research and Training Center on Research (RRTC) and Capacity Building for Minority Entities, Oklahoma City, OK
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT:
In this study we hope to identify the perceptions of obesity, diet and exercise that Hispanic young adults with disabilities have. We will analyze
sample responses on their feelings about obesity and how they feel impacts their life as well as what challenges or barriers they face as they
try to live and active and healthy life and if they are even trying. The ultimate goal is that with the gained insight we can tailor interventions for
Hispanics with disabilities.
